      ---
      
      # Value Creation Plan v3 — Cascade Care Group
      
      The bridge from entry (~~$14M EBITDA, ~$130M EV) to exit (~~$24M EBITDA, ~$220M target EV). **As of Q2-26 the plan is still off-track on EBITDA (~$11M) but the trajectory is improving:** the CFO seat is filled and the commercial engine is recovering. Each workstream has an owner, target, status (RYG), the **EV at stake**, and the **3–6 month indicators of success.** The agent ties **Estimated EV Impact**, **What Drove EV Erosion**, and **Tracking on VCP** back here.
      
      ## Value bridge (entry → target)
      
      | Lever                         | Entry | Current (Q2-26) | Target (exit) | EV at stake | Status                     |
      | ----------------------------- | ----- | --------------- | ------------- | ----------- | -------------------------- |
      | Clinic count / de-novo growth | 48    | 52              | 80            | ~$45M       | 🟡 recovering              |
      | Net collection rate           | 94%   | 92%             | 98%           | ~$25M       | 🔴 worse                   |
      | Clinician attrition           | 24%   | 28%             | 15%           | ~$20M       | 🔴 worse                   |
      | Payor mix / rate uplift       | base  | flat            | +300bps       | ~$18M       | 🟢 unblocked (CFO in seat) |
      | MSO / central back-office     | none  | live            | full          | ~$22M       | 🟢 on track                |
      | EBITDA                        | $14M  | $11M            | $24M          | —           | 🟡 stabilizing             |
      
      ---
      
      ## Workstream 1 — De-novo growth & commercial pipeline · Owner: CMO (Hale) · 🟡 recovering
      
      - **Target:** 48 → 80 clinics, fed by a repeatable de-novo / patient-acquisition pipeline at ~3x coverage.
      - **Current:** 52 clinics. After two flat quarters (Q1 pipeline coverage 1.4x vs. 3x target), Q2 was the **first quarter delivering against plan:** **net-new pipeline +38% QoQ** and **two of three target logos / partnerships closed.**
      - **What's driving the gap (EV erosion, now easing):** Pipeline was opportunistic for two quarters; modeled EV drag is **narrowing (~$1M net)** as the recovery takes hold. Held cautious pending Q3 durability.
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) net-new pipeline growth sustains into Q3; (2) recovered pipeline converts to opened/booked sites; (3) ≥ 4 disciplined openings booked for H2.
      - **Risk:** **Recovery is one quarter old — durability unproven until Q3.**
      
      ## Workstream 2 — RCM / collections · Owner: VP RCM (Tran) · 🔴
      
      - **Target:** net collection 94% → 98%; denials down.
      - **Current:** **92%** and denials **up** — moving the wrong way. **~$6M annualized cash drag.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) net collections ≥ 95%; (2) denial rate down 200bps; (3) payor-specific denial playbooks live — now supportable with payor analytics under the new CFO.
      - **Risk:** Function out-scaled by multi-payor complexity; perf plan recommended.
      
      ## Workstream 3 — Clinician retention · Owner: VP Clinical (Ortiz) + COO (Nair) · 🔴
      
      - **Target:** attrition 24% → 15%. **Current: 28%** — worse. Driving **locum/agency costs up ~$4M.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) attrition < 22%; (2) a funded retention + comp plan; (3) clinician NPS up.
      - **Risk:** Function under-resourced; **funding now unblocked with the CFO in seat** — the retention budget can finally be approved.
      
      ## Workstream 4 — Payor mix / rate improvement · Owner: CFO (Okonkwo) · 🟢 unblocked
      
      - **Target:** +300bps blended rate via payor-mix shift and contract renegotiation.
      - **Current:** **unblocked** — Naomi Okonkwo joined as CFO 2026-05-19 and now owns payor analytics and contracting. The ~$18M of bridge value tied to this workstream finally has an owner.
      - **What changed (EV impact):** Filling the CFO seat removes the single biggest overhang on the business; the operating team estimates **~+$10M EV impact** from a step-change finance function (13-week cash model rebuilt, lender relationship stabilized).
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) payor analytics stood up; (2) two contracts renegotiated; (3) durable monthly close + rolling forecast.
      
      ## Workstream 5 — MSO / central back-office · Owner: COO (Nair) · 🟢
      
      - **Target:** central scheduling, credentialing, billing, and HR shared services.
      - **Current:** **live and on track** — built and run by the COO. The steady-state engine of the deal.
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) all 52 clinics on central scheduling; (2) back-office cost-per-clinic down 10%.
      
      ## Workstream 6 — EBITDA bridge · Owner: CFO (Okonkwo) · 🟡 stabilizing
      
      - **Target:** $14M → $24M. **Current: $11M.** Mix of stalled growth, weak collections, and locum costs — now stabilizing as the CFO seat is filled and commercial recovers.
      
      ---
      
      ## EV-at-risk / EV-impact summary (people-linked)
      
      | Item                                  | Linked leader     | EV exposure / impact              | Note                                                              |
      | ------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | De-novo growth recovering             | CMO (Hale)        | ~$1M net drag (narrowing)         | First quarter delivering; durability unproven until Q3.           |
      | Payor uplift / finance engine         | CFO (Okonkwo)     | **~+$10M impact**                 | Seat filled — biggest overhang removed.                           |
      | Collections / denials behind          | VP RCM (Tran)     | ~$6M cash                         | Perf plan recommended.                                            |
      | Clinician attrition                   | VP Clinical + COO | ~$4M locum                        | Under-resourced; funding now unblocked.                           |
      | **COO retention (upside protection)** | COO (Nair)        | **~+$16M / recovery hinges here** | Retain — the catastrophic loss to avoid; the internal CEO option. |
      
      ## Headline
      
      **Stabilizing and trending up. EBITDA is still at $11M, but the two biggest people risks are resolving: the CFO seat is filled with a step-change hire (Naomi Okonkwo, ~+$10M EV) and the commercial engine is recovering under the CMO (Trevor Hale). The remaining priorities are retaining the COO (Priya Nair), proving the commercial recovery durable in Q3, and resolving the open CEO question.**

      # Cascade Care Group — Q2 2026 Board Update
      
      ## p.1 §Executive Summary
      
      Two material leadership developments this quarter. **First, the CFO seat is filled**:
      Naomi Okonkwo joined as CFO on 2026-05-19, ending the ~5-month vacancy that followed
      the prior CFO's exit. **Second, the commercial engine is showing the first real signs
      of recovery** under CMO Trevor Hale after two flat quarters.
      
      > "Filling the CFO seat removes the single biggest overhang on this business. Naomi is
      > the strongest finance hire we've made across the portfolio this year — she ran FP&A
      > and the lender relationship at a $400M revenue services platform and closed two
      > refinancings. The lender conversations are already in better hands."
      > — _M. Daugherty, Board Chair_ (p.1, §Executive Summary)
      
      The CEO question remains the open item agreed in Q1. Progress is mixed: the de-novo
      growth-discipline gate slipped again, but he executed the CFO search well and has
      stabilized the senior team.
      
      ## p.2 §CFO — Naomi Okonkwo (new hire)
      
      - Start date: 2026-05-19. Tenure: ~1 month.
      - Prior: SVP Finance at a $400M revenue managed-services platform; owned FP&A, treasury,
        and the senior lender relationship; led two refinancings.
      - First-30-day read from the operating partner is strongly positive.
      
      > "In three weeks Naomi rebuilt the 13-week cash model the prior CFO never delivered and
      > walked the lender through it herself. The bank's posture changed in the room. This is
      > a step-change for the finance function."
      > — _R. Alvarez, DAW Capital Operating Partner_ (p.2, §CFO)
      
      Risk of loss: low (just hired, strong equity package). Succession: too early to assess
      a backup; VP Finance role to be defined in H2.
      
      ## p.3 §CEO — succession question (open)
      
      > "The CFO hire was the right call and the team is steadier. But the de-novo
      > growth-discipline gate has now slipped three quarters running, and that is the gate the
      > whole margin thesis hangs on. The board wants the CEO question — and a hard date on
      > growth discipline — settled by the September meeting."
      > — _M. Daugherty, Board Chair_ (p.3, §CEO)
      
      Current state: the senior team has stabilized and the CFO search closed well, but the
      core VCP growth-discipline gate is still behind. The board's clear internal option is
      COO Priya Nair, the ready-now CEO successor; the question is whether to commit her to
      the seat or run an external process. The value-creation plan is not yet back on track.
      
      ## p.4 §Commercial — CMO Trevor Hale
      
      > "Net-new pipeline is up 38% quarter over quarter and we closed two of the three target
      > logos. After two flat quarters this is the first quarter Trevor has delivered against
      > the commercial plan."
      > — _Priya Nair, COO_ (p.4, §Commercial)
      
      Current state: improving. The commercial engine is no longer stalled, though one quarter
      does not yet make a trend — watch Q3 for durability.
      
      ## p.5 §Net Assessment
      
      - **CFO vacancy: resolved.** Largest risk on the prior review is materially mitigated.
      - **CEO: still the watch item.** PIP continues; margin gate must land by September.
      - **Commercial: early recovery.** Upgrade from "stalled," but unproven over one quarter.

      # Executive 360 Feedback — Ridgeline Freight & Logistics (H1-2026)
      
      Aggregated multi-rater feedback (1–5 across the five competency families). Verbatim comments anonymized and labeled by rater relationship. Corroborates the leadership assessment and the **healthy / on-plan** verdict, with succession as the watch item.
      
      ---
      
      ## Hank Dreyer — CEO · avg 4.3
      
      | Competency        | Self | Board | Peers | Reports |
      | ----------------- | ---- | ----- | ----- | ------- |
      | Leadership & Team | 4    | 4     | 4     | 5       |
      | Execution         | 4    | 4     | 4     | 4       |
      | Strategic Fit     | 4    | 4     | 4     | 4       |
      | Financial         | 4    | 4     | 4     | 4       |
      | Stakeholder Trust | 5    | 5     | 5     | 5       |
      
      - **Strength theme:** Universal 5 on stakeholder trust — "Customers stay because of Hank." (terminal manager)
      - **Watch theme — succession:** "We all know Hank's leaving in a couple of years. The question everyone asks is whether the customers follow Tom." (peer) — corroborates the relationship-handoff finding.
      
      ## Tom Whitman — COO · avg 4.3
      
      | Competency        | Self | Board | Peers | Reports |
      | ----------------- | ---- | ----- | ----- | ------- |
      | Leadership & Team | 4    | 5     | 4     | 5       |
      | Execution         | 5    | 5     | 4     | 5       |
      | Strategic Fit     | 4    | 5     | 4     | 4       |
      | Financial         | 4    | 4     | 4     | 4       |
      | Stakeholder Trust | 4    | 4     | 4     | 5       |
      
      - **Strength theme:** "Tom already runs the day-to-day; the title is a formality waiting to happen." (board)
      - **Watch theme — backfill:** "If Tom moves up, who runs ops? We don't have a clear answer yet." (peer) — corroborates the COO-backfill gap.
      - **Retention signal:** Strong and positive — provided the path stays firm.

      | ----------------- | ---- | ----- | ------- |

      | Strategic Fit     | 4    | 4     | 3       |

      | Stakeholder Trust | 3    | 4     | 4       |

      # Leadership Competency Framework — Ridgeline Freight & Logistics
      
      The shared assessment language. Five competency families (mirroring the methodology scorecard), each with four proficiency anchors written for an **asset-based carrier + 3PL.** Ratings roll into the scorecard dimensions and the 9-box.
      
      ## Proficiency scale
      
      | Level       | Score band | Meaning                                |
      | ----------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------- |
      | Emerging    | 1–2        | Inconsistent; a development priority.  |
      | Proficient  | 3          | Meets the bar for the role today.      |
      | Strong      | 4          | Exceeds; a model for peers.            |
      | Exceptional | 5          | Best-in-class; ready for bigger scope. |
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. Leadership & Team
      
      _Builds, retains, develops the team; for the COO, builds the bench he'll need as CEO._
      
      - **Emerging:** High turnover; carries work personally; no successor.
      - **Proficient:** Stable team; successor identified but not ready.
      - **Strong:** Bench developing; retention above the freight-industry norm; delegates real scope.
      - **Exceptional:** Deep bench; a ready-now successor; sets the standard.
      
      ## 2. Execution & Results
      
      _Delivers against plan / the VCP — density, cost-per-mile, safety, service._
      
      - **Emerging:** Misses commitments; reactive.
      - **Proficient:** Hits most commitments; some process maturity.
      - **Strong:** Consistently on/ahead of plan; repeatable across terminals.
      - **Exceptional:** Beats plan and raises the network's ceiling.
      
      ## 3. Strategic Fit (future-state)
      
      _Fit for a technology-enabled, density-optimized regional carrier + 3PL._
      
      - **Emerging:** Anchored to legacy / manual operating habits.
      - **Proficient:** Understands the future state; executing the shift.
      - **Strong:** Drives the future-state agenda across the network.
      - **Exceptional:** Defines the model; a source of thesis upside.
      - _Note:_ for the **incumbent CEO**, "future-state fit" is assessed against the retirement horizon — a declining requirement by design.
      
      ## 4. Financial Acumen
      
      _Owns the numbers — cost-per-mile, fleet capex, freight unit economics, capital._
      
      - **Emerging:** Limited ownership of the relevant economics.
      - **Proficient:** Owns the metrics; sound judgment.
      - **Strong:** Uses economics to drive decisions; clean reporting.
      - **Exceptional:** Models trade-offs the board relies on.
      
      ## 5. Stakeholder Trust
      
      _Board, shipper/customer, lender, driver, and regulator confidence._
      
      - **Emerging:** Trust uneven.
      - **Proficient:** Trusted in role.
      - **Strong:** Trusted beyond role; a go-to voice.
      - **Exceptional:** The relationship the customers / board rely on (the founder-CEO's strength).
      
      ---
      
      ## Role requirement matrix (minimum proficiency to be "thesis-ready")
      
      | Role            | Lead & Team | Execution   | Strategic Fit | Financial  | Stakeholder |
      | --------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
      | CEO (incumbent) | Exceptional | Strong      | Strong*       | Strong     | Exceptional |
      | COO (successor) | Exceptional | Exceptional | Exceptional   | Strong     | Exceptional |
      | CFO             | Proficient  | Strong      | Strong        | Strong     | Strong      |
      | VP Sales        | Strong      | Strong      | Strong        | Proficient | Strong      |
      | VP Fleet        | Proficient  | Strong      | Strong        | Strong     | Proficient  |
      | VP Safety       | Proficient  | Strong      | Proficient    | Proficient | Strong      |
      | VP People       | Strong      | Strong      | Proficient    | Proficient | Proficient  |
      
      _\*CEO Strategic-Fit requirement declines over the retirement horizon as the role transitions to the COO._
      
      ## How the framework feeds the dashboard
      
      - **9-Box** uses **Execution** (performance axis) × a blend of **Strategic Fit + Leadership & Team** (potential axis).
      - **High Potential** = Strong/Exceptional on the potential axis _and_ runway for bigger scope — at Ridgeline, the **COO** is the standout (CEO-ready).
      - The framework's most important output here is **succession readiness**: the COO's Exceptional/Strong profile is what makes the founder-CEO transition low-risk.

      # Executive Hiring & Interview Debrief Notes — Ridgeline Freight & Logistics
      
      Consolidated panel notes for executives hired at the DAW acquisition, scored against their **target scorecard** (1–5). Primary evidence behind the **Interview Performance** baseline for hired-in executives.
      
      ---
      
      ## Walter Ngiraingas — CFO (interviewed 2023-11)
      
      **Panel:** Deal Partner, CEO (Dreyer), Talent DD.
      
      | Scorecard dimension   | Score   | Note                                                   |
      | --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
      | Financial acumen      | 4       | Strong logistics-sector finance; fleet-capex planning. |
      | Execution & results   | 4       | Clean, fast close at prior carrier.                    |
      | Strategic fit         | 4       | Understands density + asset economics.                 |
      | Leadership & team     | 3.5     | Builds steady teams.                                   |
      | Stakeholder trust     | 4       | Lender-friendly; conservative.                         |
      | **Weighted baseline** | **3.9** | green                                                  |
      
      **Verbatim (Deal Partner):** "Walter is exactly the steady hand we want next to Hank, and then next to Tom. No drama, clean numbers, good on capex timing. Low-risk hire."
      
      **Decision:** Hire.
      
      ---
      
      ## Lena Osei — VP Sales / CRO (interviewed 2023-12)
      
      **Panel:** CEO (Dreyer), COO (Whitman), Talent DD.
      
      | Scorecard dimension               | Score   | Note                                        |
      | --------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
      | Execution & results (book growth) | 4       | Grew a 3PL/brokerage book at scale.         |
      | Strategic fit (3PL mix upside)    | 4       | The complement to the asset-based business. |
      | Leadership & team                 | 3.5     | Built regional sales teams.                 |
      | Financial acumen                  | 3.5     | Solid on freight unit economics.            |
      | Stakeholder trust                 | 3.5     | Credible with shippers.                     |
      | **Weighted baseline**             | **3.8** | green                                       |
      
      **Verbatim (COO Whitman):** "Lena gives us the brokerage/3PL growth lever we don't have today. She's the upside hire."
      
      **Decision:** Hire.
      
      ---
      
      ## Carla Jennings — VP Safety & Compliance (interviewed 2024-01)
      
      **Panel:** COO (Whitman), CFO (Ngiraingas), Talent DD.
      
      | Scorecard dimension                 | Score   | Note                                     |
      | ----------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
      | Execution & results (CSA/insurance) | 4       | Lowered CSA scores at a larger fleet.    |
      | Strategic fit                       | 3.5     | Knows the regulatory + insurance levers. |
      | Leadership & team                   | 3.5     | Built a safety org.                      |
      | Financial acumen                    | 3       | Connects safety to insurance cost.       |
      | Stakeholder trust                   | 3.5     | Credible with drivers + regulators.      |
      | **Weighted baseline**               | **3.6** | green                                    |
      
      **Verbatim (CFO Ngiraingas):** "Safety is a direct insurance-cost lever. Carla pays for herself if she moves the CSA scores even modestly."
      
      **Decision:** Hire.
      
      ---
      
      ## Roy Tibbets — VP People (interviewed 2024-01)
      
      **Panel:** COO (Whitman), CFO (Ngiraingas), CEO (Dreyer).
      
      | Scorecard dimension                    | Score   | Note                                         |
      | -------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
      | Execution & results (driver retention) | 3.5     | Improved driver turnover at a prior carrier. |
      | Leadership & team                      | 3.5     | Solid HR leadership.                         |
      | Strategic fit                          | 3.5     | Understands the driver-market dynamics.      |
      | Financial acumen                       | 3       | Retention/comp economics.                    |
      | Stakeholder trust                      | 3.5     | Trusted, practical.                          |
      | **Weighted baseline**                  | **3.5** | yellow                                       |
      
      **Verbatim (CEO Dreyer):** "If Roy can get our driver turnover down ten points, that's worth more than most of the cost program. It's the hardest job here."
      
      **Decision:** Hire. Focus: driver retention.
      
      ---
      
      ## Retained executives (no hire interview)
      
      - **Hank Dreyer (CEO, founder)**, **Tom Whitman (COO)**, and **Sanjay Mehta (VP Fleet)** were assessed in the org DD process (baselines 4.3, 4.1, 3.7 — see `org-due-diligence-2024`).
      - **On succession (Dreyer → Whitman):** _Verbatim (Deal Partner):_ "We are buying a great company with one timer running: Hank's retirement. The whole job is making the Tom handoff boring and orderly. Get the date and the equity right."
      
      ## Panel takeaways (deal team)
      
      1. **A low-drama, high-quality team** — every hire scored green except VP People (a high-difficulty seat, scored honestly).
      2. **The defining task is the CEO succession**, not any individual hire.
      3. **Driver retention (VP People)** is the one structurally hard mandate; resource it.

      # Leadership Re-Assessment — Ridgeline Freight & Logistics (May 2026)
      
      Independent re-assessment ~29 months post-close, scored against the **target scorecards** and **competency framework**. **Overall verdict: a mature, well-run team tracking the plan; the headline watch item is the orderly CEO succession.** For each leader: current-state score, future-state projection (vs. role target), 9-box, hi-po call, risk of loss, succession, key risks, recommended action, and confidence (**signal**).
      
      > Scale 1–5. RYG: 1–2 red, 3 yellow, 4–5 green. For the **CEO**, future state intentionally reflects the retirement horizon (a planned transition, not a miss).
      
      ---
      
      ## Hank Dreyer — CEO (founder)
      
      - **Current state: 4.2 (green).** Baseline 4.3 — essentially flat. Still the best customer and community relationships in the region; the business is humming.
      - **Future state: 3.6 (yellow)** vs. target 4.3 — **by design.** He intends to retire in **~18 months**; the future-state CEO is the COO. The yellow reflects **transition risk, not declining performance.**
      - **9-box: 1B (High performance / transition-horizon potential).** **Hi-po: n/a** (incumbent founder).
      - **Risk of loss: Planned (yellow).** Not a flight risk — a **scheduled departure** that must be managed.
      - **Succession — short-term (<6mo):** COO (Whitman), **ready-now.** **Long-term:** COO (Whitman), ready-now.
      - **Succession readiness: High (green)** — the strongest succession answer in the portfolio.
      - **Key risks:** **Customer relationships concentrated in him**; the handoff of those relationships is the real work of the transition.
      - **Signal: High (0.9).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Hank is excellent and leaving on schedule. The entire job is transferring his shipper relationships to Tom before he goes."
      - **Actionability: Medium** — _Execute a dated 18-month succession plan; begin transitioning key accounts to Whitman now._
      
      > **Evidence —** "Hank is Ridgeline to a lot of shippers; the whole game is handing that off well." — reference, org DD. // "I want a clean, dated handoff to Tom — no surprises for customers or drivers." — CEO, board deck p.6 §Succession.
      
      ---
      
      ## Tom Whitman — COO
      
      - **Current state: 4.3 (green).** Baseline 4.1 — **trending up.** Owns the density/network thesis; lane optimization and terminal efficiency are tracking ahead.
      - **Future state: 4.4 (green)** vs. target 4.4 — at target, and rising as he steps toward the CEO seat.
      - **9-box: 1A (High / High).** **Hi-po: Yes** — the **ready-now CEO successor.**
      - **Risk of loss: Low (green)** — provided the succession path stays firm and dated; the one thing that could lose him is an open-ended timeline.
      - **Succession — short-term:** VP of Operations, **developing** (his own backfill is the gating item once he moves up). **Long-term:** VP of Operations.
      - **Succession readiness: Medium (yellow)** for his own seat; **High** as CEO successor.
      - **Key risks:** **His own backfill is thin**; needs to keep building the operations bench before he vacates the COO seat.
      - **Signal: High (0.89).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Tom can run this company today. The transition is low-risk as long as we keep the date firm and start moving him into the customer relationships."
      - **Actionability: Medium** — _Confirm the dated CEO path + equity; accelerate his VP Ops successor; begin account handoffs._
      
      > **Evidence —** "Tom can run this company today; the only question is timing." — board reference, org DD. // "Network density is up and cost-per-shipment is down under Tom." — board deck p.7 §Operations.
      
      ---
      
      ## Walter Ngiraingas — CFO
      
      - **Current state: 4.0 (green).** Baseline 3.9 — steady. Clean, fast close; disciplined fleet-capex planning; lender relationships solid.
      - **Future state: 4.0 (green)** vs. target 4.0 — at target.
      - **9-box: 2A (High performance / Medium potential).** **Hi-po: No** (excellent in role; limited stated ambition beyond CFO).
      - **Risk of loss: Low (green).**
      - **Succession — short/long-term:** A controller, **developing.**
      - **Succession readiness: Medium (yellow).**
      - **Key risks:** Aging-fleet capex timing — a financial planning item, well-managed.
      - **Signal: High (0.84).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Exactly the steady hand you want through a CEO transition. No drama, clean numbers."
      - **Actionability: Low** — _Maintain; ensure he's a stabilizing presence through the succession._
      
      > **Evidence —** "Walter's close is clean and on time every month; the lender has zero concerns." — board deck p.9 §Finance.
      
      ---
      
      ## Lena Osei — VP Sales (CRO)
      
      - **Current state: 3.9 (green).** Baseline 3.8 — trending up. Growing the book and lifting the **3PL/brokerage mix** — the commercial upside lever.
      - **Future state: 3.9 (green)** vs. target 3.9 — at target.
      - **9-box: 2A (High / Medium).** **Hi-po: No** (strong in role).
      - **Risk of loss: Low (green).**
      - **Succession — short/long-term:** A sales director, **developing.**
      - **Succession readiness: Medium (yellow).**
      - **Key risks:** Freight-market softness could pressure the book — a market risk, not a leadership one.
      - **Signal: Medium (0.78).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Delivering the 3PL-growth thesis she was hired for."
      - **Actionability: Low** — _Maintain; protect the 3PL growth investment through any freight-cycle softness._
      
      > **Evidence —** "3PL/brokerage revenue is up and now ~18% of the book under Lena." — board deck p.8 §Commercial.
      
      ---
      
      ## Sanjay Mehta — VP Fleet & Maintenance
      
      - **Current state: 3.8 (green).** Baseline 3.7 — steady. **TMS + telematics rollout is on track** and cost-per-mile is improving.
      - **Future state: 3.7 (green)** vs. target 3.9 — slightly below target on the technology-adoption dimension (driver uptake of telematics is the gating item).
      - **9-box: 2B (Medium / Medium).** **Hi-po: No.**
      - **Risk of loss: Low (green).**
      - **Succession — short/long-term:** A maintenance director, **developing.**
      - **Succession readiness: Medium (yellow).**
      - **Key risks:** **Aging-fleet capex timing**; driver adoption of telematics; fuel-price exposure.
      - **Signal: Medium (0.76).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Doing the unglamorous work well. Watch the fleet-replacement capex curve."
      - **Actionability: Low** — _Maintain; align the fleet-replacement plan with the capex budget; push telematics adoption._
      
      > **Evidence —** "Telematics is live across ~70% of the fleet and idle-time is down." — board deck p.7 §Operations.
      
      ---
      
      ## Carla Jennings — VP Safety & Compliance
      
      - **Current state: 3.7 (green).** Baseline 3.6 — trending up. **CSA scores improving**, which is feeding directly into a better insurance posture.
      - **Future state: 3.7 (green)** vs. target 3.8 — near target.
      - **9-box: 2B (Medium / Medium).** **Hi-po: No.**
      - **Risk of loss: Low (green).**
      - **Succession — short/long-term:** A compliance manager, **developing.**
      - **Succession readiness: Medium (yellow).**
      - **Key risks:** A serious safety event is always a tail risk in trucking — well-managed but never zero.
      - **Signal: Medium (0.74).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Quietly turning safety into a cost advantage."
      - **Actionability: Low** — _Maintain; she is paying for herself in insurance savings._
      
      > **Evidence —** "CSA scores are down across all categories and our insurance renewal came in below plan." — board deck p.10 §Safety.
      
      ---
      
      ## Roy Tibbets — VP People
      
      - **Current state: 3.6 (yellow).** Baseline 3.5 — trending up. **Driver turnover down from ~70% to ~58%** — real progress on the structurally hardest metric in the business.
      - **Future state: 3.6 (yellow)** vs. target 3.8 — gap is the remaining distance on driver retention.
      - **9-box: 2B (Medium / Medium).** **Hi-po: No.**
      - **Risk of loss: Low (green).**
      - **Succession — short/long-term:** **Gap** both ways (the one bench gap on the team).
      - **Succession readiness: Low (red).**
      - **Key risks:** **Driver turnover still ~58%** — improved but the perennial operating risk; no bench in the people function.
      - **Signal: Medium (0.72).**
      - **Additional comments:** "Making real headway on the hardest job here; keep investing in driver retention."
      - **Actionability: Low** — _Maintain; fund the next phase of driver-retention; build a successor._
      
      > **Evidence —** "Driver turnover is down twelve points to 58% — that's worth more than most of the cost program." — board deck p.11 §People (echoing the CEO's hiring-era note).
      
      ---
      
      ## Team-level synthesis (HEALTHY / ON PLAN)
      
      - **A strong, stable team delivering the thesis.** No executive below a min bar; five of seven trending up or flat-strong.
      - **The one defining task is the orderly CEO succession** (Dreyer → Whitman) — and the succession answer is the best in the portfolio (a ready-now COO).
      - **Watch items, all well-managed:** the founder-CEO's customer-relationship handoff, the COO's own backfill, driver retention, and aging-fleet capex.
      - **Recommend:** lock the dated CEO-succession plan + COO equity now; otherwise stay the course.

      # Organizational Due Diligence — Project Ridge (Ridgeline Freight & Logistics)
      
      **Confidential — prepared for the DAW CAPITAL Investment Committee ahead of close.**
      
      ## 1. Purpose & method
      
      Assesses the leadership of Ridgeline Freight & Logistics ("Ridgeline," "the Company") and sets the **talent baseline at deal close**. Each executive was scored against the DAW target scorecard for their role (1–5 scale), via structured interview, reference calls, and review of operating records. Scores in §4 become the **Interview Performance baseline** (`basis: org-DD-at-close`).
      
      ## 2. Company & thesis context
      
      Ridgeline is a Salt Lake City–based regional LTL carrier + 3PL (~$160M revenue, ~$26M EBITDA, ~900 employees incl. ~450 drivers, ~12 terminals) across the Mountain West and Midwest. DAW's thesis is a **density + technology + margin play**: optimize lanes and the terminal network, roll out a modern TMS and telematics, complete one tuck-in terminal acquisition, cut fuel + maintenance cost per mile, improve safety/CSA scores, and expand EBITDA to ~$34M.
      
      Unlike a turnaround, this is a **"good-to-great" thesis on a well-run asset.** The dominant talent question is **CEO succession**: founder Hank Dreyer has run Ridgeline for 31 years and intends to retire within the hold period. The thesis depends on an **orderly handoff** to a credible successor.
      
      ## 3. Organizational structure at close
      
      ```
                                CEO — Hank Dreyer (founder, 31 yrs)
         ┌──────────┬─────────────┬──────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────┐
        CFO        COO         VP Sales      VP Fleet &      VP Safety &     VP People
       W. Ngiraingas T. Whitman  L. Osei      Maintenance     Compliance      R. Tibbets
                                  (S. Mehta)    (C. Jennings)
      ```
      
      The team is **complete, experienced, and stable** — the opposite profile from a typical roll-up. Bench depth is **good in operations** (the COO is a clear CEO successor) and **adequate elsewhere.**
      
      ## 4. Executive assessments & baseline scores
      
      Scale: 1 = significant concern · 3 = meets · 5 = exceptional. RYG: 1–2 red, 3 yellow, 4–5 green.
      
      ### 4.1 Hank Dreyer — CEO (founder)
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 31 years.
      - **Baseline score: 4.3 (green).** Deep industry mastery, exceptional customer and community relationships, conservative balance-sheet discipline. **Explicitly plans to retire in ~2–3 years.**
      - **Direct cost:** $880,000 total target comp.
      - **Reference signal:** "Hank _is_ Ridgeline to a lot of shippers. The whole game is handing that off well." (reference).
      - **Succession at close:** COO (Whitman), **ready-soon** — the central succession plan.
      - **Risk at entry:** **Planned-departure / succession-execution risk** is the defining issue, not performance.
      
      ### 4.2 Walter Ngiraingas — CFO
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 0 months (joins at close from a logistics-sector CFO seat).
      - **Baseline score: 3.9 (green).** Strong, steady finance leader; clean reporting; good capital-planning discipline for fleet capex.
      - **Direct cost:** $520,000.
      - **Succession at close:** A controller, developing.
      - **Risk at entry:** Low. New to the team but a known quantity.
      
      ### 4.3 Tom Whitman — COO
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 28 months (recruited two years before the sale to professionalize ops).
      - **Baseline score: 4.1 (green).** The operating engine and the **designated CEO successor.** Ran network/terminal operations at a larger carrier.
      - **Direct cost:** $560,000.
      - **Reference signal:** "Tom can run this company today. The only question is timing." (board reference).
      - **Succession at close:** A VP of Operations, developing.
      - **Risk at entry:** Low — the key is a clear, dated path to CEO so he stays for it.
      
      ### 4.4 Lena Osei — VP Sales (CRO)
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 0 months (joins at close).
      - **Baseline score: 3.8 (green).** Strong commercial leader; brings 3PL/brokerage growth experience to complement the asset-based book.
      - **Direct cost:** $400,000 (variable-weighted).
      - **Risk at entry:** Low; growing the 3PL mix is the upside she owns.
      
      ### 4.5 Sanjay Mehta — VP Fleet & Maintenance
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 4 months.
      - **Baseline score: 3.7 (green).** Owns tractors/trailers, maintenance, and the **TMS + telematics** rollout; strong on cost-per-mile.
      - **Direct cost:** $340,000.
      - **Risk at entry:** Aging-fleet capex timing; technology adoption across drivers.
      
      ### 4.6 Carla Jennings — VP Safety & Compliance
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 0 months (joins at close).
      - **Baseline score: 3.6 (green).** Owns DOT/CSA scores, insurance posture, and driver-safety programs — a value-critical seat for an asset-based carrier.
      - **Direct cost:** $290,000.
      - **Risk at entry:** Low; CSA improvement is a direct insurance-cost lever.
      
      ### 4.7 Roy Tibbets — VP People
      
      - **Tenure at close:** 0 months (joins at close).
      - **Baseline score: 3.5 (yellow).** Solid HR leader; the central challenge is the perennial one — **driver retention** (industry turnover ~70%).
      - **Direct cost:** $260,000.
      - **Risk at entry:** Driver turnover is the recurring operating risk.
      
      ## 5. Bench & succession summary at close
      
      | Seat      | Internal successor at close | Readiness                  |
      | --------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------- |
      | CEO       | COO (Whitman)               | **Ready-soon / ready-now** |
      | CFO       | Controller                  | Developing                 |
      | COO       | VP of Operations            | Developing                 |
      | VP Sales  | Sales director              | Developing                 |
      | VP Fleet  | Maintenance director        | Developing                 |
      | VP Safety | Compliance manager          | Developing                 |
      | VP People | None                        | Gap                        |
      
      ## 6. Key talent risks at entry (for the IC)
      
      1. **CEO-succession execution** — the founder will retire in the hold; the handoff to the COO is the defining talent task.
      2. **Driver retention** — the structural operating risk for any asset-based carrier.
      3. **Aging-fleet capex** — a financial/operational risk owned by the VP Fleet, not a leadership-quality risk.
      
      ## 7. Recommendation
      
      Proceed to close. **Talent is a clear thesis enabler** — an experienced, stable team with a ready successor. Day-1 priorities: agree a **dated CEO-succession plan** (Dreyer → Whitman), lock the COO with a clear path and equity, and set driver-retention targets. Re-assess at 18 months with succession-readiness as the headline metric.
      
      _— DAW CAPITAL Human Capital Diligence, 8 December 2023_

      # Ridgeline Freight & Logistics — Q2 2026 Board Deck
      
      > Slide-structured source. Page/section markers (e.g. "p.6 §Succession") are the citation anchors other documents reference. Speaker attributions appear in _Notes_.
      
      ---
      
      ## p.1 — Cover
      
      **Ridgeline Freight & Logistics · Q2 2026 Board Review**
      DAW CAPITAL portfolio company · Prepared for the Board · 2 June 2026
      
      ---
      
      ## p.2 — Agenda
      
      1. Headline & scorecard
      2. Financial performance
      3. Value-creation plan status
      4. Operations & technology
      5. Commercial
      6. Finance
      7. Safety
      8. People & driver retention
      9. CEO succession
      10. Risks & asks
      
      ---
      
      ## p.3 — Headline
      
      - EBITDA **$30.5M** (entry $26M; target $34M) — **on track.**
      - Lane density **+6%**; cost-per-mile **-4%**; CSA scores **improving.**
      - Driver turnover **58%** (from 70%; target 55%) — **improving.**
      - Tuck-in terminal **in diligence.**
      - **No red workstreams.** Headline watch item: **orderly CEO succession.**
      
      _Notes (CEO):_ "Best year the company's had. The one big thing on my mind is handing this off cleanly."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.4 — Quarterly financial summary
      
      | Metric                | Q3-25 | Q4-25 | Q1-26 | Q2-26 |
      | --------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
      | Revenue ($M)          | 39.0  | 39.8  | 40.4  | 41.0  |
      | EBITDA ($M)           | 28.2a | 29.1a | 29.9a | 30.5a |
      | Cost-per-mile index   | 100   | 98    | 97    | 96    |
      | Driver turnover (TTM) | 66%   | 63%   | 60%   | 58%   |
      | 3PL mix               | 14%   | 15%   | 17%   | 18%   |
      
      _(a = annualized run-rate)_
      
      ---
      
      ## p.5 — VCP status (RYG)
      
      | Workstream                  | Owner                       | Status          |
      | --------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------- |
      | Lane density / network      | COO Whitman                 | 🟢 on track     |
      | TMS + telematics            | VP Fleet Mehta              | 🟢 on track     |
      | Tuck-in terminal            | CEO Dreyer + CFO Ngiraingas | 🟢 in diligence |
      | Cost-per-mile (fuel/maint.) | VP Fleet Mehta              | 🟢 on track     |
      | CSA / insurance             | VP Safety Jennings          | 🟢 on track     |
      | Driver retention            | VP People Tibbets           | 🟡 improving    |
      | CEO succession              | Board + CEO                 | 🟡 watch        |
      
      ---
      
      ## p.6 — §Succession
      
      - Founder-CEO intends to retire in **~18 months.**
      - **COO (Whitman) is the ready-now successor** (see talent review).
      - Plan: dated handoff + COO equity; begin transitioning top accounts now.
      
      _Notes (CEO, H. Dreyer):_ "I want a clean, dated handoff to Tom — no surprises for customers or drivers. We should start moving the big accounts to him this year."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.7 — §Operations & technology
      
      - **Network density up; cost-per-shipment down under the COO.**
      - **Telematics live across ~70% of the fleet; idle-time down.**
      
      _Notes (COO, T. Whitman):_ "Network density is up and cost-per-shipment is down. Telematics adoption is the grind, but the data's already paying off."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.8 — §Commercial
      
      - **3PL/brokerage revenue up to ~18% of the book** under the VP Sales — the upside lever working.
      
      _Notes (VP Sales, L. Osei):_ "Brokerage is now ~18% of the book; it gives us a growth lever beyond the asset base."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.9 — §Finance
      
      - EBITDA $30.5M, on track.
      - **Clean, on-time close every month; lender has zero concerns.**
      - Tuck-in financing being structured.
      
      _Notes (CFO, W. Ngiraingas):_ "The close is clean and on time every month; the lender has zero concerns. We're structuring the tuck-in financing now."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.10 — §Safety
      
      - **CSA scores down across all categories; insurance renewal came in below plan.**
      
      _Notes (VP Safety, C. Jennings):_ "CSA scores are down across all categories and our insurance renewal came in below plan — safety is now a cost advantage."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.11 — §People (driver retention)
      
      - **Driver turnover down twelve points to 58%** (target 55%).
      - Driver-pay / quality-of-life program in phase 2.
      
      _Notes (VP People, R. Tibbets):_ "Driver turnover is down twelve points to 58% — that's worth more than most of the cost program."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.12 — Executive compensation (direct cost)
      
      | Executive         | Role                   | Total target comp |
      | ----------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- |
      | Hank Dreyer       | CEO                    | $880,000          |
      | Walter Ngiraingas | CFO                    | $520,000          |
      | Tom Whitman       | COO                    | $560,000          |
      | Lena Osei         | VP Sales               | $400,000          |
      | Sanjay Mehta      | VP Fleet & Maintenance | $340,000          |
      | Carla Jennings    | VP Safety & Compliance | $290,000          |
      | Roy Tibbets       | VP People              | $260,000          |
      
      ---
      
      ## p.13 — Risks & asks to the board
      
      1. **CEO succession** — approve a dated 18-month plan and the COO equity grant; begin account handoffs now.
      2. **COO backfill** — endorse accelerating the VP Operations successor before the COO steps up.
      3. **Tuck-in** — approve proceeding from diligence to LOI.
      4. **Driver retention** — fund phase 2 of the driver program.
      
      _Notes (CEO):_ "Nothing here is on fire. The job is to make the handoff boring and keep the flywheel turning."

      # Ridgeline Freight & Logistics — Q2 2026 Board Deck
      
      > Slide-structured source. Page/section markers (e.g. "p.6 §Succession") are the citation anchors other documents reference. Speaker attributions appear in *Notes*.
      
      ---
      
      ## p.1 — Cover
      **Ridgeline Freight & Logistics · Q2 2026 Board Review**
      DAW CAPITAL portfolio company · Prepared for the Board · 2 June 2026
      
      ---
      
      ## p.2 — Agenda
      1. Headline & scorecard
      2. Financial performance
      3. Value-creation plan status
      4. Operations & technology
      5. Commercial
      6. Finance
      7. Safety
      8. People & driver retention
      9. CEO succession
      10. Risks & asks
      
      ---
      
      ## p.3 — Headline
      - EBITDA **$30.5M** (entry $26M; target $34M) — **on track.**
      - Lane density **+6%**; cost-per-mile **-4%**; CSA scores **improving.**
      - Driver turnover **58%** (from 70%; target 55%) — **improving.**
      - Tuck-in terminal **in diligence.**
      - **No red workstreams.** Headline watch item: **orderly CEO succession.**
      
      *Notes (CEO):* "Best year the company's had. The one big thing on my mind is handing this off cleanly."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.4 — Quarterly financial summary
      | Metric | Q3-25 | Q4-25 | Q1-26 | Q2-26 |
      |---|---|---|---|---|
      | Revenue ($M) | 39.0 | 39.8 | 40.4 | 41.0 |
      | EBITDA ($M) | 28.2a | 29.1a | 29.9a | 30.5a |
      | Cost-per-mile index | 100 | 98 | 97 | 96 |
      | Driver turnover (TTM) | 66% | 63% | 60% | 58% |
      | 3PL mix | 14% | 15% | 17% | 18% |
      
      *(a = annualized run-rate)*
      
      ---
      
      ## p.5 — VCP status (RYG)
      | Workstream | Owner | Status |
      |---|---|---|
      | Lane density / network | COO Whitman | 🟢 on track |
      | TMS + telematics | VP Fleet Mehta | 🟢 on track |
      | Tuck-in terminal | CEO Dreyer + CFO Ngiraingas | 🟢 in diligence |
      | Cost-per-mile (fuel/maint.) | VP Fleet Mehta | 🟢 on track |
      | CSA / insurance | VP Safety Jennings | 🟢 on track |
      | Driver retention | VP People Tibbets | 🟡 improving |
      | CEO succession | Board + CEO | 🟡 watch |
      
      ---
      
      ## p.6 — §Succession
      - Founder-CEO intends to retire in **~18 months.**
      - **COO (Whitman) is the ready-now successor** (see talent review).
      - Plan: dated handoff + COO equity; begin transitioning top accounts now.
      
      *Notes (CEO, H. Dreyer):* "I want a clean, dated handoff to Tom — no surprises for customers or drivers. We should start moving the big accounts to him this year."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.7 — §Operations & technology
      - **Network density up; cost-per-shipment down under the COO.**
      - **Telematics live across ~70% of the fleet; idle-time down.**
      
      *Notes (COO, T. Whitman):* "Network density is up and cost-per-shipment is down. Telematics adoption is the grind, but the data's already paying off."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.8 — §Commercial
      - **3PL/brokerage revenue up to ~18% of the book** under the VP Sales — the upside lever working.
      
      *Notes (VP Sales, L. Osei):* "Brokerage is now ~18% of the book; it gives us a growth lever beyond the asset base."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.9 — §Finance
      - EBITDA $30.5M, on track.
      - **Clean, on-time close every month; lender has zero concerns.**
      - Tuck-in financing being structured.
      
      *Notes (CFO, W. Ngiraingas):* "The close is clean and on time every month; the lender has zero concerns. We're structuring the tuck-in financing now."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.10 — §Safety
      - **CSA scores down across all categories; insurance renewal came in below plan.**
      
      *Notes (VP Safety, C. Jennings):* "CSA scores are down across all categories and our insurance renewal came in below plan — safety is now a cost advantage."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.11 — §People (driver retention)
      - **Driver turnover down twelve points to 58%** (target 55%).
      - Driver-pay / quality-of-life program in phase 2.
      
      *Notes (VP People, R. Tibbets):* "Driver turnover is down twelve points to 58% — that's worth more than most of the cost program."
      
      ---
      
      ## p.12 — Executive compensation (direct cost)
      | Executive | Role | Total target comp |
      |---|---|---|
      | Hank Dreyer | CEO | $880,000 |
      | Walter Ngiraingas | CFO | $520,000 |
      | Tom Whitman | COO | $560,000 |
      | Lena Osei | VP Sales | $400,000 |
      | Sanjay Mehta | VP Fleet & Maintenance | $340,000 |
      | Carla Jennings | VP Safety & Compliance | $290,000 |
      | Roy Tibbets | VP People | $260,000 |
      
      ---
      
      ## p.13 — Risks & asks to the board
      1. **CEO succession** — approve a dated 18-month plan and the COO equity grant; begin account handoffs now.
      2. **COO backfill** — endorse accelerating the VP Operations successor before the COO steps up.
      3. **Tuck-in** — approve proceeding from diligence to LOI.
      4. **Driver retention** — fund phase 2 of the driver program.
      
      *Notes (CEO):* "Nothing here is on fire. The job is to make the handoff boring and keep the flywheel turning."

      # Target Scorecards by Role — Ridgeline Freight & Logistics
      
      Role-level scorecards used to score candidates at hire / org DD and to define the **future-state bar** each seat must clear to deliver the value-creation plan. Scale 1–5. **Target** = thesis-ready score. **Min bar** = below this is a red flag. Weights sum to 100%.
      
      > The gap between an executive's current score (leadership assessment) and the **Target** here drives **Future State Performance** and **Actionability**. For PC3 the dominant future-state factor is the **CEO-succession horizon**.
      
      ---
      
      ## CEO — Hank Dreyer (incumbent, planned transition)
      
      | Dimension                              | Weight | Target  | Min bar | Why it matters                                                                |
      | -------------------------------------- | ------ | ------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | Stakeholder trust (shippers/community) | 30%    | 4.5     | 3.5     | Customer relationships are the moat.                                          |
      | Execution & results                    | 20%    | 4.0     | 3.0     | Keep the business humming through transition.                                 |
      | Strategic fit (future-state CEO)       | 20%    | 4.5     | 3.0     | **Declining over horizon — he is retiring; the future-state CEO is Whitman.** |
      | Leadership & team (succession)         | 20%    | 4.5     | 3.5     | An orderly handoff is the #1 job.                                             |
      | Financial acumen                       | 10%    | 4.0     | 3.0     | Balance-sheet discipline.                                                     |
      | **Blended target**                     |        | **4.3** |         |                                                                               |

      | Dimension                        | Weight | Target  | Min bar | Why it matters                       |
      | -------------------------------- | ------ | ------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
      | Financial acumen (capex/capital) | 30%    | 4.0     | 3.0     | Fleet capex + tuck-in financing.     |
      | Execution & results              | 25%    | 4.0     | 3.0     | Clean, fast close; lender reporting. |
      | Strategic fit                    | 20%    | 4.0     | 3.0     | Density + asset economics.           |

      ---
      
      ## How to read this against performance
      
      - **Interview Performance** (baseline) was scored against these same weights at hire / org DD.
      - **Future State Performance** = projected score vs. the **Target** column (gap to target). For the **CEO**, future-state intentionally **declines** over the horizon because the role transitions to the COO — this is a _plan_, not a performance miss.
      - No PC3 executive is currently below a Min bar — consistent with the "healthy/on-plan" verdict. The only structural watch items are **CEO-succession timing** and **driver retention.**

      ---
      
      # Value Creation Plan v2 — Ridgeline Freight & Logistics
      
      The bridge from entry (~~$26M EBITDA, ~$210M EV) to exit (~~$34M EBITDA, ~$300M target EV). **As of Q2-26 the plan is on track.** Each workstream has an owner, target, status (RYG), the **EV at stake**, and the **3–6 month indicators of success.** The agent ties **Estimated EV Impact**, **What Drove EV Erosion** (minimal here), and **Tracking on VCP** back to this document.
      
      ## Value bridge (entry → target)
      
      | Lever                                 | Entry | Current (Q2-26) | Target (exit) | EV at stake | Status       |
      | ------------------------------------- | ----- | --------------- | ------------- | ----------- | ------------ |
      | Lane density / network optimization   | base  | +6%             | +12%          | ~$35M       | 🟢 on track  |
      | TMS + telematics rollout              | none  | 70% live        | full          | ~$25M       | 🟢 on track  |
      | Tuck-in terminal acquisition          | 0     | in diligence    | 1             | ~$30M       | 🟢 on track  |
      | Fuel + maintenance cost-per-mile      | base  | -4%             | -8%           | ~$20M       | 🟢 on track  |
      | CSA / insurance cost                  | base  | improving       | -15%          | ~$12M       | 🟢 on track  |
      | Driver turnover                       | 70%   | 58%             | 55%           | ~$15M       | 🟡 improving |
      | EBITDA                                | $26M  | $30.5M          | $34M          | —           | 🟢 on track  |
      | **CEO succession (Dreyer → Whitman)** | —     | planning        | complete      | risk-mgmt   | 🟡 watch     |
      
      ---
      
      ## Workstream 1 — Lane density & network optimization · Owner: COO (Whitman) · 🟢
      
      - **Target:** +12% density / cost-per-shipment improvement. **Current: +6%, on pace.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) two underutilized lanes consolidated; (2) cost-per-shipment down a further 3%; (3) terminal-level dashboards live.
      
      ## Workstream 2 — TMS + telematics · Owner: VP Fleet (Mehta) · 🟢
      
      - **Target:** modern TMS + full telematics. **Current: ~70% of fleet live; idle-time down.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) telematics ≥ 90% of fleet; (2) idle-time down a further 10%; (3) driver-adoption training complete.
      - **Watch:** driver adoption is the gating item (see 360).
      
      ## Workstream 3 — Tuck-in terminal acquisition · Owner: CEO (Dreyer) + CFO (Ngiraingas) · 🟢
      
      - **Target:** one terminal acquisition to extend the network. **Current: in diligence, on track.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) LOI → close; (2) financing locked (CFO); (3) 90-day integration plan ready.
      
      ## Workstream 4 — Fuel + maintenance cost-per-mile · Owner: VP Fleet (Mehta) · 🟢
      
      - **Target:** -8% cost-per-mile. **Current: -4%.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) preventive-maintenance compliance ≥ 95%; (2) fuel-card + routing program savings booked; (3) aging-fleet replacement plan aligned to capex.
      
      ## Workstream 5 — Safety / CSA → insurance · Owner: VP Safety (Jennings) · 🟢
      
      - **Target:** -15% insurance cost via CSA improvement. **Current: CSA improving; renewal came in below plan.**
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) CSA scores down across all BASIC categories; (2) preventable-accident rate down; (3) next renewal modeled below plan.
      
      ## Workstream 6 — Driver retention · Owner: VP People (Tibbets) · 🟡
      
      - **Target:** turnover 70% → 55%. **Current: 58%** — improving, not yet at target.
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) turnover < 56%; (2) driver-pay/quality-of-life program phase 2 live; (3) driver NPS up.
      
      ## Workstream 7 — CEO succession · Owner: Board + CEO (Dreyer) · 🟡 (watch)
      
      - **Target:** orderly, dated handoff to the COO (Whitman) within ~18 months.
      - **Why it's the headline item:** ~all of the customer-relationship value sits with the founder; the EV case assumes a clean transition.
      - **3–6 month indicators of success:** (1) dated succession plan + COO equity locked; (2) top-20 accounts begin transitioning to Whitman; (3) COO's own VP Ops successor in development.
      
      ---
      
      ## EV-at-risk summary (people-linked)
      
      | Item                     | Linked leader                | EV exposure     | Note                                                         |
      | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
      | CEO-succession execution | CEO (Dreyer) → COO (Whitman) | transition-risk | The defining watch item; mitigated by a ready-now successor. |
      | Driver turnover          | VP People (Tibbets)          | ~$15M           | Improving; the structural operating risk.                    |
      | Aging-fleet capex / fuel | VP Fleet (Mehta)             | ~$20M           | Well-managed; market exposure.                               |
      | COO backfill             | COO (Whitman)                | bench-depth     | Develop before he vacates the seat.                          |
      
      ## Headline (no material EV erosion)
      
      **On plan across the board. EBITDA up from $26M to $30.5M toward a $34M target. The two watch items are the orderly CEO succession (mitigated by a ready-now COO) and driver retention (improving). No workstream is red.**

    status: Completed · exit 0
      # Backing services for the Second Brain build — Postgres+pgvector, MinIO, ElasticMQ.
      # They start EMPTY: schema, buckets, and queues are yours to create (see STACK.md).
      # Extend this file freely — add your app's services here, or run them on the host.
      
      name: second-brain
      
      services:
        db:
          image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
          environment:
            POSTGRES_USER: brain
            POSTGRES_PASSWORD: brain
            POSTGRES_DB: secondbrain
          ports:
            - "5432:5432"
          volumes:
            - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
          healthcheck:
            test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U brain -d secondbrain"]
            interval: 3s
            timeout: 3s
            retries: 20
      
        minio:
          image: minio/minio:latest
          command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
          environment:
            MINIO_ROOT_USER: minio-root
            MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: minio-secret
          ports:
            - "9000:9000" # S3 API  (SDK: endpoint http://localhost:9000, forcePathStyle: true)
            - "9001:9001" # web console
          volumes:
            - miniodata:/data
          healthcheck:
            test: ["CMD", "mc", "ready", "local"]
            interval: 3s
            timeout: 3s
            retries: 20
      
        queue:
          image: softwaremill/elasticmq-native:latest
          ports:
            - "9324:9324" # SQS-compatible API (SDK: endpoint http://localhost:9324; create queues via CreateQueue)
      
      volumes:
        pgdata:
        miniodata:

## Assistant

Fixed the workspace export resolution.

`@second-brain/api` now explicitly exports its Hono app/type surface from `apps/backend/package.json`, and `AppType` is exported from `src/app.ts` without starting the server during a type-only frontend import.

Verified with frontend TypeScript, lint, and full build.

## User

Let's add a first sanity check between the frontend and the backend.

The frontend should be able to do a call to the backend, maybe with a dump route. The backend should be able to respond with a dump data inside it. We should be able to have the typings that are correct between the frontend and the backend with the RPC. And that will make sure that the frontend can talk to the backend.

## Assistant

I’ll add a typed `/dump` Hono endpoint, enable local development CORS, and render its response through a TanStack Query call in the frontend. Then I’ll run both services and verify the request over HTTP.

      export const app = new Hono();
      export type AppType = typeof app;

        return c.json({ error: 'Internal server error' }, 500);

## User

Let's work on the frontend routing. We now have funds and portcos. we can already put all of this in the frontend routes.

- root index page : Will list all the funds available
- fund/$fundSlug : Will be the main fund dashboard
- fund/$fundSlug/portco : portcos list linked to that fund
- fund/$fundSlug/portco/$portcoSlug : Same dashboard as the fund one, but scoped to portco

      ---
      name: frontend-design
      description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
      license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
      ---
      
      # Frontend Design
      
      Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.
      
      ## Ground your designs in the subject matter
      
      If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
      
      ## Design principles
      
      For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.
      
      Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.
      
      Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
      
      Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.
      
      Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
      - Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
      - Using all caps for labels.
      - Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.
      
      Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.
      
      Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.
      
      Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
      
      ## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique
      
      For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
      1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
      2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
      3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
      4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
      5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.
      
      All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
      
      Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
      - Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
      - Type: the typefaces and their roles.
      - Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
      - Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.
      
      Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.
      
      When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.
      
      ## Restraint and self-critique
      
      Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
      
      ## More on writing in design
      
      Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
      
      Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.
      
      Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
      
      Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.
      
      Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

      import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
      import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'
      import { api } from '../lib/api'
      
      export const Route = createFileRoute('/')({ component: Home })
      
      function Home() {
        const dump = useQuery({
          queryKey: ['api', 'dump'],
          queryFn: async () => {
            const response = await api.dump.$get()
      
            if (!response.ok) {
              throw new Error(`API request failed with status ${response.status}`)
            }
      
            return response.json()
          },
          retry: false,
        })
      
        return (
          <main className="mx-auto mt-24 w-[min(42rem,calc(100%-2rem))]">
            <p className="text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.2em] text-accent">DAW Capital</p>
            <h1 className="mt-4 font-serif text-5xl tracking-tight text-ink">Second Brain</h1>
            <p className="mt-5 text-muted">A defensible record of the people decisions that matter.</p>
            <section className="mt-10 rounded-sm border border-rule bg-card p-6" aria-live="polite">
              <p className="text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.16em] text-muted">
                API sanity check
              </p>
              {dump.isPending ? <p className="mt-3 text-ink">Checking the API…</p> : null}
              {dump.isError ? <p className="mt-3 text-failure">{dump.error.message}</p> : null}
              {dump.data ? (
                <div className="mt-3">
                  <p className="font-medium text-accent">{dump.data.message}</p>
                  <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-muted">
                    {dump.data.service} · {new Date(dump.data.checkedAt).toLocaleTimeString()}
                  </p>
                </div>
              ) : null}
            </section>
          </main>
        )
      }

      slug: string
      code: string
      name: string
      sector: string
      location: string
      status: 'on pace' | 'needs attention' | 'on plan'
      focus: string
    }
    
    export type Fund = {
      slug: string
      name: string
      description: string
      portcos: PortfolioCompany[]
    }
    
    export const funds: Fund[] = [
      {
        slug: 'daw-capital',
        name: 'DAW Capital',
        description: 'Lower-middle-market private equity',
        portcos: [
          { slug: 'vantage-managed-services', code: 'PC1', name: 'Vantage Managed Services', sector: 'IT / managed services', location: 'Denver, CO', status: 'on pace', focus: 'Retain the CTO and build the finance bench.' },
          { slug: 'cascade-care-group', code: 'PC2', name: 'Cascade Care Group', sector: 'Healthcare provider services', location: 'Portland, OR', status: 'needs attention', focus: 'Stabilize leadership around COO retention and the finance bench.' },
          { slug: 'ridgeline-freight-logistics', code: 'PC3', name: 'Ridgeline Freight & Logistics', sector: 'Transportation & logistics', location: 'Salt Lake City, UT', status: 'on plan', focus: 'Execute the founder-CEO succession and backfill the COO.' },
        ],
      },
    ]
    
    export function getFund(slug: string) {
      return funds.find((fund) => fund.slug === slug)
    }
    
    export function getPortco(fundSlug: string, portcoSlug: string) {

    import { createFileRoute, notFound } from '@tanstack/react-router'
    import { Dashboard } from '../../../../components/dashboard'
    import { getFund, getPortco } from '../../../../lib/organizations'
    
    export const Route = createFileRoute('/fund/$fundSlug/portco/$portcoSlug')({ component: PortcoDashboard })
    
    function PortcoDashboard() {
      const { fundSlug, portcoSlug } = Route.useParams()
      const fund = getFund(fundSlug)
      const portco = getPortco(fundSlug, portcoSlug)
    
      if (!fund || !portco) throw notFound()
    
      return <Dashboard fund={fund} portco={portco} />
    }

    import { Link, createFileRoute, notFound } from '@tanstack/react-router'
    import { getFund } from '../../../../lib/organizations'
    
    export const Route = createFileRoute('/fund/$fundSlug/portco/')({ component: PortcoList })
    
    function PortcoList() {
      const { fundSlug } = Route.useParams()
      const fund = getFund(fundSlug)
    
      if (!fund) throw notFound()
    
      return <main className="fund-index"><header className="index-heading"><p className="breadcrumb"><Link to="/fund/$fundSlug" params={{ fundSlug: fund.slug }}>{fund.name}</Link></p><h1>Portfolio companies</h1><p>Choose a company to work within its scoped record.</p></header><section className="fund-list" aria-label={`${fund.name} portfolio companies`}>{fund.portcos.map((portco) => <Link key={portco.slug} to="/fund/$fundSlug/portco/$portcoSlug" params={{ fundSlug: fund.slug, portcoSlug: portco.slug }} className="fund-row"><span><strong>{portco.name}</strong><small>{portco.sector}</small></span><span className={`status status-${portco.status.replaceAll(' ', '-')}`}>{portco.status}</span></Link>)}</section></main>
    }
